title: Failure envelope
description: The failure a command refused with, printed on stdout when the invocation asked for --json (ADR-0021; src/errors.js). stderr stays empty in that mode, and the human path is unchanged when it does not. Exit codes are identical in both modes: the classification lives in `code`, never in the exit status, so adding this envelope breaks no existing caller. The envelope carries no repository content, file contents, or commit messages (NFR-SEC-02). Pre-dispatch failures — a conflicting or malformed global flag, consumed before the per-command options are parsed — keep prose on stderr, because no output mode is known yet.

code.description: A member of the closed vocabulary published in docs/schemas/errors.md, whose runtime authority is ERROR_CODES in src/errors.js. It names why the command refused, so a caller can branch without matching English. Adding a code is additive inside v1; removing one, or changing what it means, is a version bump. `null` never appears from a vcs-lab raise site — every one is required to carry a code, which test/error-envelope.test.js enforces statically — and is permitted here only so an unexpected non-CliError failure can still be reported in the same shape rather than escaping it.

message.description: The same sentence the human path prints after the `vlab: ` prefix. Intended for a person; automation should branch on `code`.

details.description: The supplementary text the human path prints on its own line, often Git's own output. Empty when there is none. Free text: ADR-0021 deliberately left structured detail members unfrozen.

exitCode.description: The process exit status this failure produced, restated so a caller reading only stdout does not have to observe it separately.
